copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Panama v Croatia in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Tuesday, and the model and the market disagree on the Croatia side by +12.2pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

Elo numbers going in: Panama 1560, Croatia 1860. That's a 300-point lead for Croatia — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Panama to win at 13%, the draw at 12%, and Croatia to win at 75%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Croatia sits at 75% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Panama to win at 12%, the draw at 22%, and Croatia to win at 62%. The Croatia side trades at 62% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of −167. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 75%, +12.2pp wider.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Croatia the lower bound is 66%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.9pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

News will move the prior. With kickoff roughly 33 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. On a Pick this wide, it would take material news — a missing star, a tournament dropout, a venue change — to collapse the gap below the +3pp threshold; on the narrower side of the field, a single refresh can flip Pick to Pass. Either way, the Desk re-publishes after each refresh and does not recommend a trade.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +12.2pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On every meaningful read, Croatia look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 75% vs market 62% — a +12.2pp gap on the favourite side.
copy.title: Panama v Croatia · the model leans Croatia
